name: Cynthia A. Chestek
title: Professor of Biomedical Engineering, Robotics, and Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
department: Biomedical Engineering; Robotics; Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
fitReason: Strong applied-AI intersection in motor-intent decoding, signal nonstationarity, learned interfaces and real-time prosthetic control. A software or existing-data decoding study could be tightly scoped; clinical contact or implant experimentation must never be assumed available to a short-term visitor.

physicalEvidence.summary: Full February 2026 primary methods distinguish two experiments. Two participants controlled a virtual hand for grip-classification evaluation; separately, one participant used an actual Ossur iLimb Quantum hand plus Fillauer powered wrist rotator to perform a physical coffee-making task. A trained linear-discriminant EMG classifier selected grips/wrist actions, with a 150 ms decision threshold and 500 ms velocity ramp; xPC Target sent commands through CAN. This supplies learned physical execution, but the physical functional test is a one-person case, not a two-person robotic-hand trial or a fully autonomous neural-network manipulator.

shortVisit.summary: The official indexed lab email policy addresses prospective PhD applications, current Michigan undergraduates and master’s students continuing a BME517 class project into directed research. It does not state an external-master short-visit offer. The live lab/email-policy fetches returned 403, so indexed official content is labeled accordingly.
